exposure: lifestyle factors (stress, sleep deprivation, dental hygiene, diet)
cohort: 56 OB/GYN female residents and 41 age-matched controls
finding: Although OB/GYN residents reported more adverse lifestyle factors, their obstetric and gynecological outcomes were comparable to controls, with residency and parity being independently associated with a higher pregnancy rate.
mod_finding: Despite differences in lifestyle factors, there were no significant differences in rates of cesarean deliveries between OB/GYN residents and controls.
